meta.title: Second Law of Thermodynamics — Full Lecture
meta.description:
Complete lecture on the second law of thermodynamics, entropy and the carnot cycle.

Join the course: https://example.com/course
telegram: https://example.com/telegram

segs.utf8: ok so in today's lecture we will finish the second law of thermodynamics
we will start with the basics and slowly move to the carnot cycle
before that a quick recap of the first law
the first law is just energy conservation for a gas
so now let's move on to the second law of thermodynamics
the second law tells us the direction of heat flow
heat always flows from a hotter body to a colder body
kelvin planck and clausius statements are the two versions
as we discussed earlier when we looked at heat engines this matters a lot
next topic is entropy
entropy is a measure of the disorder of the system
the change in entropy is the integral of dq over t
for a reversible process this is exact
now let's look at heat engines
a heat engine takes heat from a hot reservoir
and converts part of it into work
the efficiency is one minus q two by q one
no engine can be one hundred percent efficient
let's now discuss the carnot cycle
the carnot cycle has four reversible processes
two isothermal and two adiabatic
the efficiency depends only on the two temperatures
next we come to refrigerators and heat pumps
a refrigerator is the reverse of a heat engine
the coefficient of performance is the useful effect by the work input
moving on to the solved examples now
first question is a carnot engine operating between two temperatures
we will find the efficiency from the temperatures directly
second question is about entropy change in mixing
you have to integrate carefully here
finally let's do a quick revision
remember entropy always increases for an irreversible process
and the carnot efficiency is the maximum possible
